out_items.name: Wiping cloths properly used and stored

violations.title: Wiping Cloths Stored in Sanitizer Solution
violations.observation: Wet wiping cloths used for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces were observed stored on the counter.
violations.corrective_action: Wet wiping cloths are to be used for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces and are to be held in a chemical sanitizer solution at the appropriate concentration between uses. PIC placed wet wiping cloths in sanitizer solution.

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Observed utensils in use stored in a water container at the cook line with the water temperature at 111F.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. EHS instructed PIC on proper storage of food utensils in food preparation area. PIC removed utensils from the water container and properly cleaned and sanitized them.

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, Design/Construction
violations.observation: Milk crate(s) found used for the following purpose(s): Observed milk crates used to elevate tamarind and store utensils.
violations.corrective_action: Milk crates, soda crates, and/or bread racks are not designed to store or elevate food, equipment, utensils, clean linens, and single-service items. Provide only ANSI-certified (such as NSF-listed) shelving units, storage units, or dunnage racks. EHS instructed PIC to discontinue use of milk crates as storage. PIC removed the tamarind and utensils from the milk crates and placed them on approved shelving.

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation and was not observed to be date marked: cooked chickpeas, tomato sauce (prepared onsite) in 3 DR prep cooler; salsa (cooked onions), tomato sauce (prepared onsite) in 2 DR UPR refrigerator ; cooked brown rice, salsa in 2 DR UC cooler.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. EHS discussed the proper date marking food items after 24 hours: all prepared foods sitting under refrigeration for more than 24 hours required labels with dates. The food shall be sold or discarded no later than 6 days from the date of preparation. PIC placed date markings on all aforementioned foods during the inspection.

violations.observation: The following equipment is not operating properly and/or is in poor repair: Observed burnt-out bulbs under a grease hood.

violations.title: Food Protection Manager - Accredited Program
violations.observation: It shall be unlawful to operate a food establishment unless it is under the immediate control of a certified food manager who has shown proficiency through passing an accredited examination. PIC was not able to provide a certified food manager certificate.
violations.corrective_action: Please obtain a certified food managers certificate from an accredited program prior to the follow up inspection.

out_items.name: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events

violations.title: Clean-up of vomiting and diarrheal events
violations.observation: The food establishment does not have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events.
violations.corrective_action: A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the food establishment. The procedures shall address the specific actions employees must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of employees, consumers, food and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. EHS provided the written vomiting/diarrhea clean up policy. Ensure staff are trained on the policy before the follow up.

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation and was not observed to be date marked: The following homemade food items are not being date marked as required: tomato chutney, samosa with cooked peas, onion sauce, lentil paste.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. EHS discussed the proper date marking food items after 24 hours: all prepared foods sitting under refrigeration for more than 24 hours require labels with dates. The food shall be sold or discarded no later than 6 more days from the date of preparation. Ensure correction before the follow up. The follow up inspection will be conducted within 10 days. PIC

violations.title: RTE TCS Commercially Processed Food, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is commercially processed is not used or discarded within 24 hours of when the original container was opened and is not observed to be date marked: commercial yogurts that were placed in deli containers and stored in 2 DR flat-top cooler more than 24 hours ago.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety commercially processed foods when opened and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of the original container was opened. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. This date cannot exceed any manufacturer determined 'use-by' date based on food safety. EHS discussed date marking with management. All food sitting under refrigeration for more than 24 hours requires labels with dates. Please provide corrections prior to the follow up inspection. SAI SARAVANA BHAVAN (Inspection Date: 03/28/2025) Page 2 of 3

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name
violations.observation: The following food items that are not easily identified by appearance were observed without a label: squeeze bottles of oil, water, sauces.
violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc. PIC labeled all squeeze bottles throughout the kitchen.
